soundness_flags.label: def:sample-split-estimator; thm:pooled-wald-certified
soundness_flags.one_line: A positive uniform Jacobian singular-value margin does not make the within-graph minimum-distance minimizer unique, while the estimator gives no tie-breaking rule; add a certified global injectivity/unique-minimizer condition and a measurable deterministic selector before defining a single asymptotic law.

soundness_flags.label: oeq:certifiable-design-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: “Practically bounded refinement” is undefined and refining M or other controls changes Xi itself; specify the admissible finite design/refinement set and a numerical resource bound.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Consequence 6 gives the exceptional non-identifiable bivariate Poisson form; Definition 10 defines pairwise identifiability and Lemma 11 identifies the multivariate DAG from the joint law under it.
The paper studies aggregation recoverability and reports restrictive linear/affine preservation conditions; it does not present a known-composition multi-pool PGF certificate.
The article supplies rigorous floating-point and interval-verification foundations, rather than a causal PGF graph-separation and precision procedure.
Taylor models provide rigorous function enclosures and can support branch-and-bound global search.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the certificate prove or directly validate global injectivity of every within-graph moment map, then specify a deterministic measurable argmin selector and thread that premise into the Wald theorem.

Replace the open question’s qualitative “practically bounded” language with an explicit finite candidate design class, budget metric, and Pareto frontier for (graph gap, Jacobian margin, N_req, arithmetic cost).

Produce one independently checkable nontrivial certified instance, including all DAG-box exclusions, tail receipts, and the resulting precision budget, to demonstrate that the algorithmic kernel is more than a generic interval-arithmetic composition.

recommended_next_step: Revise the estimator/certificate interface to certify global within-graph identification and formalize the design-frontier search domain, then return the field-tier certificate kernel for review.
